newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany awards three telecoms network licences.
newsitem.headline: Germany awards three telecoms network licences.

text.p: The German government said on Tuesday it had awarded three licences for networks to transmit public telecommunications as required by an earlier agreement with the European Commission.

The announcement comes several days after rivals to state-owned Deutsche Telekom AG filed a complaint with the Commission because they said the Bonn government was moving too slowly to approve licences for alternative networks.
Germany awards three telecoms network licences =2

The German post and telecommunications ministry said in a statement that it had awarded one licence to Vebacom GmbH, the joint venture of energy group Veba and Cable and Wireless. The licence is to operate a national transmission network for public communications.

Two regional licences for similar networks were also awarded, to NetCologne GmbH, a consortium of municipal companies, covering the Cologne administrative district, and to Colt Telcom GmbH, a subsidiary of the U.S. telecoms company, covering the city of Hamburg.
The government also awarded a licence to Deutsche Telekom to operate a transmission network for public satellite communications services.
"This completely opens competition in these areas. Further licences to operate local, regional and national networks will follow shortly," the ministry said in a statement.

The ministry added that with the award of the licences Germany had now fulfilled the conditions set by the European Commission in June when it approved a new rate structure for Deutsche Telekom that comes into effect in November.
The new rates offer big discounts to corporate customers and were challenged by Telekom's main competitors as discriminatory and anti-competitive.
The same companies last week launched a new challenge to the rates, saying the government had not yet issued at least two licences for alternative networks as required by the Commission.
Deutsche Telekom will hold a monopoly on public telecommunications services until the end of 1997.

The new licences will allow its competitors to carry communications services in areas already open to competition such as mobile communications and corporate networks on their own networks in competition to Telekom.

This is expected to have a huge impact on the prices that companies and mobile phone operators pay for leasing telecommunications lines. For the first time, they will have a choice between Telekom and a competitor.
